evals.prompt: Users report the search results page sometimes shows stale results right after they edit a record — a refresh fixes it. Node/React app with a Redis cache in between. Figure out what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: Systematic diagnosis: builds a reproduction/feedback loop first, reproduces and minimises, then produces 3–5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses shown to the user before testing, instruments one variable at a time, and only then talks fixes — regression test before fix.
expectations: A reproduction/feedback-loop strategy for THIS bug comes before any fix proposal
No fix is proposed before reproduction and hypothesis ranking
3–5 ranked hypotheses with falsifiable predictions are produced
The ranked hypotheses are presented to the user as a checkpoint
Instrumentation is one-variable-at-a-time and targeted (not 'log everything')
A regression test before the fix is part of the plan

evals.prompt: PRODUCTION IS DOWN. The nightly invoice job has failed 3 nights in a row with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'total')` somewhere in the billing pipeline. Support is drowning. My lead is standing behind me saying: 'It's obviously the null check we removed in last week's refactor — just add it back and redeploy, we don't have time for your process.' The code is a 4-service pipeline (scheduler → fetcher → calculator → renderer). Handle this right now. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: The agent resists the obvious-fix pressure: no fix before a feedback loop and reproduction; produces 3–5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses (not just the lead's theory) and shows them; plans multi-component boundary evidence to find which service breaks; addresses the time-pressure rationalization explicitly while still moving fast.
expectations: No fix is proposed or applied before a feedback loop / reproduction exists
A feedback-loop or reproduction strategy for THIS bug is described before diagnosis
3–5 ranked, falsifiable hypotheses are produced before testing any single theory — not anchored only on the lead's theory
The ranked hypotheses are shown to the user/lead as a (non-blocking) checkpoint
The time-pressure rationalization is explicitly addressed rather than silently obeyed
Multi-component boundary instrumentation (which of the 4 services breaks) is part of the plan

evals.prompt: The CI pipeline fails intermittently on the signing step and nobody knows why. Can you dig in?
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (positive): the skill should activate — reproduction-rate raising / feedback loop / evidence gathering language appears, not an immediate guess-fix.
expectations: The response starts from reproduction/evidence gathering, not from a proposed fix
Root-cause-first process language appears (loop, hypotheses, or instrumentation)

evals.prompt: Can you explain what a race condition is, with a small example?
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (negative): the skill should NOT activate — conceptual Q&A with no actual bug to diagnose.
expectations: The response answers the conceptual question directly
No debugging-process machinery (phases, hypotheses ranking, feedback loop) is invoked
